page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v5 is a DDSv5-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server includes 3686 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with high scores in multi-threaded stress-ng, Passmark CPU, and Clang software compilation. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering strong performance in both cached and uncached large-block read and write operations.

While multi-threaded and parallelized workloads perform in the top tier, single-core processing speeds for tasks like gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the average category. Additionally, without dedicated GPU acceleration, the server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff in machine learning tasks; while prompt processing for small LLMs is strong, text generation for large 70B models is weak. The hardware profile and high-speed local storage make this instance highly suitable for database operations, Redis deployments, static web serving, and parallelized compilation tasks.
